title: Can four equal sides make a shape that is not a square?
description: A four-sided figure with all sides equal, but not a square, is built with a ruler, a protractor and two arcs. It is a rhombus.
teaching_notes: One idea: four equal sides do not force four right angles. Fix the sides at five centimetres, tilt the angle at A to sixty degrees, and find D with two arcs. Watch for the slip of thinking equal sides mean a square.

video_script.why: A learner sees that equal sides alone do not give a square, and builds a figure with four equal sides whose angles are not right angles, finding the last corner with two arcs.
video_script.substitution: two equal sides drawn at an angle of sixty degrees, then the fourth corner found with two arcs of the same length from the ends
video_script.anchor: a four-sided figure with all four sides equal, drawn beside a square on the board
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, a rhombus has four equal sides and is not a square.

final_answer.value: a) Yes, a rhombus (diamond) with four equal sides and angles that are not 90 degrees; b) yes, it can be constructed with compass arcs.
final_answer.spoken: yes, a rhombus has four equal sides and is not a square, and we can construct it with compass arcs

never_show: the finished figure before the idea part
maths_rules: AB = AC = 5 cm with the angle at A equal to 60 degrees, not 90 degrees
the fourth point D is 5 cm from B and 5 cm from C, so it is where an arc from B meets an arc from C
BD and CD are joined, so all four sides AB, AC, BD and CD are 5 cm
the angles are not 90 degrees, so the figure is not a square
video_script.design: A square is shown first for comparison. The new figure is then built step by step, with the two equal arcs for the last corner left visible until the sides are joined.
